messages:
Maya Chen: Heads up — onboarding Kairo17b (int4) to staging. Seeing transient OOMs on bursty short-chat workload. P95 latency fine but GPUs fragment after ~300-600 short requests.
Liam O'Connor: Saw that in the canary run this morning. Pattern: lots of small generations (max_new_tokens=512) -> KV churn -> mem spikes -> OOMs on dense schedules.
Sofia Patel: Can you paste the current serve config? curious about batch timeout / slow-start.
Maya Chen: Current canary config (what we used):
```
model: kairo17b-int4
max_new_tokens_default: 512
batching:
  max_batch_tokens: 8192
  batch_timeout_ms: 12
warmup:
  slow_start_percent: 0.0
memory:
  kv_compaction_interval_s: 300
```
Maya Chen: Suspect two things: (1) default max_new_tokens too high for short-chat traffic, (2) no slow-start / cwnd => big bursts cause fragmentation.
Devon Reddy: +1. Propose we try a combined approach: lower default max_new_tokens for hosted routing, add a gradual congestion-window-style ramp (cwnd) for in-flight token budget, and a small "cache_cushion" that reserves a fraction of slots to reduce fragmentation.
Liam O'Connor: Proposed quick patch (canary) I tested locally: lowered max_new_tokens to 256, batch_timeout_ms=6, enable cwnd ramp and run KV compaction more aggressively.
```
model: kairo17b-int4
max_new_tokens_default: 256
batching:
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  batch_timeout_ms: 6
  gradual_cwnd_ramp: true
memory:
  cache_cushion: 0.06   # reserves 6% of kv slots to avoid tight packing
  kv_compaction_interval_s: 120
warmup:
  slow_start_percent: 0.2
  slow_start_requests: 40
```
Kai (eng-runtime): cwnd idea fits natural throttling. Rough algorithm: on new connection set cwnd = base_tokens; each successful completion -> cwnd += alpha; on OOM/failure -> cwnd *= beta (0.6); cap by max_batch_tokens. Keeps the number of concurrently reserved KV slots smoother.
Sofia Patel: Will this affect quality? dropping default max_new_tokens could truncate long completions for some customers.
Maya Chen: We'll keep route-level overrides. Hosted default -> 256 for chat routes. Customers that need longer can explicitly set max_new_tokens or we route them to dedicated pools.
Devon Reddy: Also add a small proactive compaction hook: after N short requests (N=50) do an in-place KV compaction on that instance to reduce fragmentation. That + cache_cushion should help median memory headroom.
infra-bot: Scheduled nightly compaction job for kairo17b-int4 on staging at 02:00 UTC. Job id: compaction-3076543210-01
Liam O'Connor: I'll push the canary with the patch (cwnd + cache_cushion + lower max_new_tokens) and run traffic replay. Will capture trace + heap dumps if OOM occurs.
Sofia Patel: I'll add a small eval: suite of short-chat prompts + a few long-format prompts to ensure no quality regressions with int4 quant + cwnd throttling.
Maya Chen: Action items: (1) Liam deploy canary and run 2h replay; (2) Devon add compaction hook and metric for "cushion_usage"; (3) Sofia add eval and compare Rouge/BLEU+LM-score; I'll monitor OOM logs and latency SLOs. :thumbsup: 
Kai (eng-runtime): If we still see tail OOMs, next step is per-instance slot reservation (soft vs hard) and a tiny per-request KV-priority bit to let short requests reuse slots preferentially.
Maya Chen: Thanks all — will update thread with canary link & logs.
